subject: Priv Deploy: Helm/Ansible modular review + OPA admission checks for GitOps
messages:
From: Tara Voss <tara@acme-fin.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@acme-fin.com
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy preflight: Helms + Ansible + OPA checks

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. As we prepare the move from staged VPC to prod VPC for the Redwood private deployment, the security team has two asks before we sign off on the GitOps pipeline:

1) Ensure Helm charts are validated for prohibited hostNetwork/elevated capabilities and that values.yaml does not contain plaintext secrets.
2) Run Ansible idempotency tests against our staging clusters and produce a dry-run report we can attach to the audit.
3) Add an OPA admission policy step (rego) to the GitHub Actions pipeline so PRs that try to allow privileged containers are blocked.

Can Redwood provide a short checklist and an example GH Actions workflow with an OPA admission gate? Also, we need at least one full CI dry-run report (helm template + ansible --check) that we can attach to our SOC2 artifact bundle.

Target timeline: we'd like the artifacts and an update by EOD Wednesday, 3 June. Is that feasible?

Appreciate it,
Tara
Lead, Infra Security
ACME Financial

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Tara Voss <tara@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Jun 2026 09:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy preflight: Helms + Ansible + OPA checks

Tara —

Thanks for the clear asks. We're on it. Quick summary of what we'll provide by EOD Wed:

- A one-page IAC review checklist (PDF) covering Helm anti-patterns, required values constraints, and Ansible idempotency sanity checks.
- A sample GitHub Actions snippet that runs: helm lint -> helm template (policy scan) -> ansible --check -> OPA gate using conftest/rego.
- A dry-run artifact bundle: CI logs + helm-values audit (we'll redact secrets), and an ansible --check report.

Small clarifications before we run:
- Do you want the OPA gate as a pre-merge check only, or also enforced on the cluster via admission controller? (We can supply both options; cluster admission will need kube-apiserver webhook config on your end.)
- For ansible --check I need a staging credentials token (read-only) or a kubeconfig that uses your staging service account. Can ops share a short-lived kubeconfig?

I'll loop in Marcus for the dry-run and Irene for the Helm values audit.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Tara Voss <tara@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Jun 2026 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy preflight: Helms + Ansible + OPA checks

Quick update — I ran a full dry-run against ACME staging this morning with the following steps (details attached):

Steps executed:
- helm repo update; helm lint --strict ./charts/redis-cache
- helm template ./charts/api -f ci/values-staging.yaml | kubeconform -strict -summary
- ansible-playbook site.yml -i inventory/staging --check --diff
- conftest test -p policies/ <(helm template ./charts/api -f ci/values-staging.yaml)

Findings (high-level):
- Helm: one chart used hostPort in a test helper subchart (test-helper) — not present in production charts but should be removed from chart templates.
- Values: a few ci/values-staging.yaml entries contained credentials placeholders (not plaintext creds) but we recommend moving all to sealed secrets or external secret manager.
- Ansible: playbook was idempotent in 94% of tasks; two tasks flagged that change is expected on first run (package installs) but subsequent runs were idempotent.
- OPA/Conftest: policy 'no-privileged-containers' caught a kube Job in test-helper using securityContext.privileged: true.

Artifacts attached: ci-dryrun-report.txt (log), helm-values-audit.yaml (sanitized), and a short remediation note.

Cc'ing Irene for the proposed Helm template changes and for the GH Actions workflow we should check in.

— Marcus
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: ci-dryrun-report.txt (plain text), helm-values-audit.yaml (yaml)
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Tara Voss <tara@acme-fin.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 11:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy preflight: Helms + Ansible + OPA checks

Tara —

I've drafted a crisp checklist (attached as iac_review_checklist.pdf) with explicit gate points to add to your GitOps repo:

1) PR must pass helm lint and helm template | kubeconform (deny on failures).
2) No hostNetwork/hostPort/privileged containers allowed in rendered manifests.
3) Values file must reference only secret keys (external) — block if any key looks like a secret literal.
4) Run ansible --check; fail pipeline if idempotency regressions exceed configurable threshold (we recommend 1% for initial gating).
5) Run conftest with our shared rego policies; we provide both pre-merge conftest action and an admission controller bundle if you choose cluster enforcement.

I've included a reference GitHub Actions job snippet in the PDF and the link to the PR with the conftest policies on our side: https://github.com/redwood-inference/priv-deploy/pull/412

If you're aligned with the checklist, next steps: ops shares a short-lived kubeconfig for the staging cluster and we'll run one more dry-run to generate the final artifact bundle for your SOC2 evidence.

Regards,
Irene Choi
Infrastructure Security, Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Tara Voss <tara@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deploy preflight: Helms + Ansible + OPA checks

Tara — thanks for the quick turnaround on access. We got the short-lived kubeconfig and ran the verification smoke one more time. Deliverables uploaded:

- iac_review_checklist.pdf (detailed gates + GH Actions snippet)
- ci-dryrun-report.txt (sanitized logs, includes helm lint/kubeconform output + ansible --check summary)
- helm-values-audit.yaml (sanitized values with notes to move to external secrets)
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/priv-deploy/pull/412 (conftest policies + sample action)

Immediate recommendations:
- Remove test-helper hostPort from chart templates and re-run helm template to ensure conftest passes.
- Add a pre-merge action that runs conftest and kubeconform; enforce via branch protection.
- For cluster-level enforcement, ops should open a ticket with their k8s admins to accept our webhook manifest; we can provide a Helm chart for the admission config.

Would you like us to present the artifacts to your auditors next Thursday (10 Jun) or just hand them the bundle? We can do either — happy to join their call.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1-415-555-0133
Redwood Inference
